text:
maria: Quick heads-up — nightly perf showed a ~45% CPU regression on the prefill+decode path when opportunistic handshake batching was enabled for small token-budget jobs. Full profile attached in CI artifact but TL;DR looks like KV cache churn + kernel crossover thrash.

aj: yikes. which change triggered it? the new kernel affinity heuristic from yesterday?

maria: yeah that commit + the token-budget soft ceil we landed. repro on rtx-pool2 with 8k seq synthetic load.

sam: can you paste the flame graph snapshot? last time that helped locate the back-and-forth between kernels.

maria: pasted snippet here:```
CPU%  Stack
18%   runtime.kv_primer -> kv_cache.evict_if_needed -> kernel_switcher.select()
14%   handshake.batcher -> queue.handoff -> kernel_switcher.select()
11%   decode.generator -> kernel_fallback.copy_state
```

cleo: from that it sounds like kernel_selector is oscillating between int8 fused and fp16 matmul based on transient batch shapes. tiny prefill batches hit int8 path, decode batches prefer fp16 for higher throughput, and handshake logic forces rapid context switches.

tim: additional note: token-budget soft ceil means many requests now start with a prefill budget of 6-8 tokens then immediately request decode batches. The scheduler tries to opportunistically merge but ends up creating lots of 1-2 token decode microbatches. That increases kernel churn.

aj: can we gate opportunistic handshake batching behind a min-batch-size or min-token-budget? e.g., avoid merging decode-phase batches if combined batch would produce >30% kernel diversity (rough heuristic).

maria: proposed experiment config (quick):```json
{
  "handshake_opportunistic": true,
  "min_tokens_to_merge": 16,
  "kernel_switch_hysteresis_ms": 12,
  "kv_primer_window_ms": 50
}
```

sam: I like min_tokens_to_merge. also add a small kernel_switch_hysteresis so we don't flip kernels for microbatches. 12ms seems reasonable as a start.

cleo: one more: bump kv_primer_window to 100ms when handshake_opportunistic is true. gives KV cache time to warm and reduces eviction pressure. But measure memory pressure as side-effect.

maria: ran an A/B with min_tokens_to_merge=16, hysteresis=12ms, kv_primer_window=100ms. Results: tail latency +7% (expected), p50 unchanged, CPU down 30% vs the opportunistic-on baseline, and kernel switches down from ~4.1M -> 0.9M per hour. Looks promising.

aj: any regression on high-concurrency sustained workloads?

maria: small regressions under >1200 concurrent streams — our min_tokens_to_merge delays merging and increases queue length; that caused a few request timeouts in the stress harness.

tim: maybe make min_tokens_to_merge dynamic: scale down when queue depth > Q_HIGH (e.g., 200) and up when queue depth low. pseudo:```
if queue_depth > 200: min_tokens_to_merge = 8 else min_tokens_to_merge = 16
```

mar ia: typo in your name above : )

maria: heh thanks :) yes dynamic min_tokens sounds good. also we should add a metric: kernel_switch_rate per GPU and a kv_eviction_rate gauge so we can alert preemptively.

cleo: agree. also add an integration test that fakes alternating prefill/decode patterns and asserts kernel_switch_rate < threshold. catches this class early.

sam: can we roll this as canary feature flag? rollout plan: 1) opt-in internal only (2 nodes), 2) 10% traffic for 24h, check kernel_switch_rate & kv_evictions, 3) 50% then full.

maria: I'll draft the flag + config PR. tagging @infra-bot to kick off canary pool creation.

infra-bot: canary pool provisioning requested by maria. ETA ~18m.

aj: one last thought — revisit kernel selection thresholds: instead of strict rules, use a tiny RL-style bandit to pick kernel based on recent effectiveness per batch-shape. But that's larger scope. For now, heuristics + hysteresis + dynamic merge rules should mitigate.

maria: agreed. I'll open a tracking ticket for the bandit idea. PR incoming with metrics, dynamic min_tokens, and hysteresis knobs. will paste link when ready. :thumbsup:

last message: maria: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/+/PR-3274 — contains config + test harness + dashboards. please review when you can.
